method: Reconciled scratchpad and durable collection review first; read effective EC3 source at table captions and footers; inspected relevant code and assertion bodies. No tests run in this shard.

source_locations.details: If Split is absent, preferred orientation follows View: D/no value horizontal, T vertical; no splitter for H/C. The available-area collection splitter itself is introduced as a may in §12.3.5.1.
Caption, Type, S and A rows all appear on this page. The preceding sort-type rules and NOTE 3 lexical implementation dependency are on physical 467/printed452.

Type, Background, CardBackground, CardBorder begin on physical467/printed452; PrimaryText and SecondaryText continue on physical468/printed453. All values are optional arrays of three DeviceRGB numbers in [0,1].

Caption, Type, Direction and Position are on this page. The prose immediately preceding says display may be divided into navigation and a preview of the initial/current selected collection document; user adjustment is permitted.

errata.annotation_inventory: Neither page has StrikeOut/Caret/Text errata annotations. The only markup objects are link annotations to Table 156 and Table 153. Relevant effective renumbering #477 for the later Collection navigators material is already addressed in the collections shard and is not a correction to Tables 156-158.
errata.effective_scope: No EC3 correction to the audited sort, colors, or split cells was found on these pages.

features.title: Entries in a collection sort dictionary

cells.source: Optional; if present shall be CollectionSort.
cells.implementation: Collection parser reads /Sort without using /Type as a performability guard.
cells.assertions: No reader rejection obligation is inferred from this producer-validity cell.

cells.source: Required name or array of names; each identifies a parent Schema field. Array entries break ties in sequence until unique or exhausted.
cells.implementation: collection::sorted_keys builds keyed comparator list in file order and applies successive fields.
cells.assertions: Model test a_second_field_breaks_a_tie_and_no_sort_states_no_order uses numeric primary and file-name secondary values with /A [true false]; it asserts the exact reversed secondary result. Host test a_collection_lists_its_files_in_the_order_table_153_states exercises visible row ordering for a single text key.

cells.source: Optional boolean applies ascending/descending; array entries correspond index-wise to /S. Extra array entries are ignored, missing entries are assumed true, default is true.
cells.implementation: Sort::ascending broadcasts a one-element boolean, otherwise reads the indexed bool and returns true when absent; extra booleans have no named field to affect.
cells.assertions: Existing tests cover /A absent and one-field /A false, plus exact two-field /A [true false]. They do not assert the specified short-array case where a later key defaults true. Proposed public consumer draft isolates it while also testing date ordering.

cells.source: §12.3.5.1 says numbers ascending by numeric magnitude and dates by chronological instant. Text is lexical ascending, with NOTE 3 calling lexical order an implementation dependency.
cells.implementation: sortable/compare dispatch by Schema FieldKind; number uses numeric comparison, date parses PDF dates and compares instants, text compares decoded strings.
cells.assertions: Public host rows prove lexical filename order; model tests prove numeric ascending/descending. Existing email example parses a Date schema and sort direction but does not sort actual date values. No date-order consumer assertion found. Proposed exact-xref PDF1.7 draft compares offset-bearing dates with literal UTC chronology, tied under the numeric primary key.

cells.source: The table guarantees successive sort keys through unique order or exhaustion; it specifies no extra tie-break after key exhaustion.
cells.implementation: The repository chooses original EmbeddedFiles tree order for remaining ties; missing values are placed after present values in both directions.
cells.assertions: These are documented owner decisions in ADR 1168, not ISO-required semantics; existing numeric test demonstrates its missing-value choice. No new defect asserted.

features.parent_verdict: Confirmed B76: /A [false] incorrectly broadcasts false to the second key. /A [false true] orders dates correctly. Sort parsing collapses scalar false and one-element array into the same Vec<bool>; ascending() broadcasts singleton values.

features.title: Entries in a collection colors dictionary

cells.source: Every color entry is optional. Each specified color is a DeviceRGB triple in [0,1]. Table 153 calls /Colors a suggested set; its NOTE says it is recommended that a layout use the colors provided.
cells.implementation: pdf-model::collection::colours reads each known three-component array. Current shared host does not apply these values; panel::unused_furniture reports that the viewer uses its own colors. Native widgets keep platform styling.
cells.assertions: Model test a_navigator_names_layouts_in_the_order_the_file_prefers_them reads Background [1,1,1], and host test the_presentation_entries_this_window_does_not_draw_are_named_out_loud confirms a colors request is surfaced in a message. Neither asserts rendered RGB.

features.verdict: Not a SHALL defect: color use is recommended and owner ADRs 1168/1252 choose platform colors. Describe it as a declined recommendation with a stated product rationale, not as a hard reader requirement or a claim that colors are applied.

features.title: Entries in a collection split dictionary

cells.source: Optional; if present shall be CollectionSplit.
cells.implementation: Parsed only when a /Split dictionary exists; reader does not use /Type as a rejection gate.
cells.assertions: Producer rule, no mandatory reader rejection claim.

cells.source: Optional PDF2.0 H, V or N. N means no split and the entire window region shall be dedicated to file navigation.
cells.implementation: SplitDirection preserves H/V/N; only N affects window geometry via panel::whole_window. H/V is not used to create a preview pane because the product does not implement collection preview splitting.
cells.assertions: Host mapping test table_158s_n_gives_the_whole_window_to_the_file_navigation_view checks N true, no Split false, and hidden View H false. `unused_furniture` test checks H/V is named. GTK/Qt/UI consumer callsites were traced; this shard did not find host pixel assertions for this condition.

cells.implementation: Model clamps an out-of-range value; current host does not apply it because it does not present the Collection's two-area preview split.
cells.assertions: Existing model example asserts an invalid Position 250 is clamped to 100. That is robustness behavior on a producer-invalid value, not a valid-input conformance witness. No rendered-position assertion found.

features.related_table_153: When /Split is absent, preferred orientation is determined by /View: D or no value indicates horizontal, T indicates vertical; no splitter for H/C. This is distinct from a default /Direction value inside a present split dictionary, for which Table 158 states no explicit default. Current product does not present a collection-file preview splitter, so omission is a product capability choice; do not treat the dictionary fields alone as a mandatory request to add such UI.

scope_limits: This is a Table 156-158 cell review, not complete §12.3.5 certification. It does not repeat the prior CI columns, folders, initial-document, or navigator-layout findings.
No whole-ADR certification is made. Table 157's recommendation is weighed separately from SHALL; Table 158's /N rule is distinguished from the optional preview splitter.
No test execution claim is made in this shard.
parent_execution: B76: short A array FAIL; explicit mixed directions, explicit all descending and scalar false controls PASS. T164 records the independent date chronology controls. Parent execution supersedes scratch-only statements below.
